seo agency cost vs freelancer cost
h1: SEO agency vs freelancer: the ₹60,000 crossover
metaTitle: SEO Agency vs Freelancer: The ₹60,000 Crossover
metaDescription: SEO agency vs freelancer comes down to hidden costs. Tools and writers add about ₹25,000 to a freelancer quote. The crossover sits close to ₹60,000.
answer: A freelance SEO in India charges ₹15,000–₹60,000 a month for one person's part-time attention. Tools and writers add roughly ₹25,000 on top, and link work usually isn't included at all. That puts the real crossover near ₹60,000 a month — below it a good freelancer wins, above it an agency covers more per rupee.
takeaways: A freelancer quote prices **one person's hours**. An agency retainer prices hours plus tools, writers, an editor, link outreach and cover. Compare the scopes, not the numbers.
**₹25,000/month is the floor** for the tools and writing a freelancer expects you to supply. In a content-heavy programme it's closer to ₹50,000.
Link outreach is the line item that almost never appears in a sub-₹40,000 freelance quote, and it's the one that takes longest to compound.
Below ₹40,000/month a good freelancer beats a cheap agency. That's not a compliment to freelancers — it's what a ₹25,000 agency retainer actually is.

sections.h2: What Indian SEO freelancers charge in 2026
body: These are the bands you'll meet, not survey data. Rates track two things: years of real ownership of a P&L-relevant number, and whether the person freelances full-time or moonlights around a job. The second one matters more than anyone admits — a moonlighter's Tuesday belongs to their employer.
Cities matter less than they used to. A senior freelancer in Kochi and one in Gurgaon quote within a few thousand rupees of each other, because both are pricing against the same remote client pool.
bullets: **₹10,000–₹25,000/mo** — one to three years' experience, usually generalist. On-page edits, a few blogs, Search Console screenshots in the report. Fine for a five-page local site, nothing more.
**₹25,000–₹50,000/mo** — three to six years. Can run a real audit, has opinions about internal linking, will usually write or brief content. This is the band most founders actually hire from.
**₹50,000–₹1,20,000/mo** — seven years plus, often ex-agency lead, frequently at capacity and taking two or three clients. Genuinely good, genuinely hard to book.
**₹800–₹4,000/hr** for hourly work, and **₹15,000–₹75,000** for a one-off audit depending on site size and whether you get a call afterwards or just a PDF.

callout.title: Ask what "full-time" means
callout.body: "I'm full-time freelance" and "you're one of my six retainers" are both true statements about the same person. Ask how many clients they carry and how many hours a month yours gets. A number under fifteen is not a retainer, it's a subscription to advice.

sections.h2: The line items a freelancer quote leaves out
body: This is where the comparison actually happens. A freelancer sells their hours. Everything those hours need in order to produce anything is your problem, and most quotes don't say so out loud — not out of dishonesty, but because the freelancer assumes you know.

bullets: Add the middle rows and you get **₹23,000–₹53,000 a month** of work that has to happen and isn't in the freelance number. ₹25,000 is the floor, not the average.

The link row is the sharpest one. A freelancer can advise on links. Running outreach at any real volume is a full job, and nobody does it properly inside a ₹35,000 retainer that also covers technical and content.

body: Take a competent mid-band freelancer at ₹35,000/month. Add the conservative ₹25,000 of tools and writing you now buy separately. You're at ₹60,000 a month for one person's part-time attention, four articles, and no link capacity.

At ₹75,000 an agency gives you a technical specialist, a content team with an editor, someone running outreach, and an account lead who owns a number — plus the tools, plus somebody who knows your account when the main person is on leave. Per deliverable, it's cheaper. Per hour of senior human attention, it isn't, and it never will be.
So the crossover isn't a cliff. It's the point where the question changes from "can I get this done cheaper?" to "am I paying agency money for freelancer coverage?"

callout.title: Where we sit
callout.body: Our SEO retainers start at ₹75,000/mo, with smaller sites from ₹40,000 — the full breakdown is on [our pricing page](/pricing). At ₹40,000 we're competing directly with a good freelancer and we say so; below that, hire the freelancer.

sections.h2: The risk that appears in neither quote
body: A freelancer is a single point of failure attached to a human being with a life. That's not a criticism — it's arithmetic. One person can get ill, get a full-time offer, get a client who pays double, or simply go quiet for three weeks in December.

The failure mode is rarely dramatic. It's a Slack message that takes four days, then a week, then a month of "sorry, been swamped". By the time you accept it's over, your content calendar has a hole in it, nothing is documented, and the Search Console property is verified to a Gmail address you don't control.
None of that means don't hire a freelancer. It means hire one with the exit already built.
numbered: **You own every account.** GA4, Search Console, the CMS, the rank tracker, the domain registrar. Grant access; never receive it.
**One shared folder, updated monthly.** Audit, keyword map, content calendar, link targets, what shipped. If the work only exists in their head, you're renting their memory.
**A written monthly report** with the same three numbers every month. Not screenshots.
**Thirty days' notice, both ways, in writing.** Any freelancer who resists this is telling you something useful.

sections.h2: What a freelancer genuinely does better
body: Agencies have an obvious incentive to skip this section, so here it is in full. There are situations where hiring one is straightforwardly the right call, and the honest ones will tell you so during the pitch.
bullets: **Small and local.** A single-location clinic, restaurant or studio needs a correct Google Business Profile, a fast site, honest service pages and reviews. That's one competent person's job and an agency retainer is overkill.
**A deep single specialism.** A brilliant technical SEO on a replatform beats a generalist pod. Same for penalty diagnostics and log-file work.
**Short, defined projects.** Audits, migrations, schema builds. Fixed scope, fixed price, nobody has an incentive to extend the engagement.
**Founder-led content.** If you're the subject-matter expert and you'll write, you need direction and editing, not a content team. That's a freelancer's sweet spot.
**Speed.** No account manager, no approval chain, no weekly call about the weekly call. Decisions happen in a WhatsApp message.

sections.h2: The verdict, and how to test it before committing
body: Under ₹40,000 a month, hire a good freelancer. A ₹25,000 agency retainer is a freelancer with an office to pay for, and you'll get less of them than you would get direct. That's the uncomfortable version of the same advice you'll find in [what an SEO agency really costs](/cost/seo-agency-cost).

Over ₹60,000 a month, or the moment you need technical work, content and links happening in the same month, the agency wins on coverage. One person cannot run outreach, write four articles and diagnose a crawl budget problem in the same fortnight, and if they say they can, look at the outreach.

Between ₹40,000 and ₹60,000, run the test rather than the argument. Buy a paid audit from both — ₹20,000–₹50,000 each — with the same brief and the same access. You'll learn more from two audits than from ten pitch calls, because an audit is the one deliverable you can judge without waiting six months. If you want the shape of the work either would be doing, [how SEO agencies work](/answers/how-do-seo-agencies-work) lays out the sequence.

callout.title: The question that ends most pitches
callout.body: "What happens if it doesn't work?" A freelancer usually has no answer. Most agencies have a paragraph. We freeze your trailing-90-day qualified organic leads on day one and keep working free until we beat that baseline — never a promised ranking position, because nobody controls Google's index.

versus.verdict: Under ₹40,000/month, or on a single-location local site, hire a good freelancer — over ₹60,000/month, or the moment technical work, content and link outreach all need to happen in the same month, the agency delivers more per rupee.

faqs.q: How much does a freelance SEO cost in India?
faqs.a: ₹10,000–₹25,000/month for one to three years' experience, ₹25,000–₹50,000 for three to six, and ₹50,000–₹1,20,000 for a senior ex-agency specialist. Hourly runs ₹800–₹4,000 and a standalone audit ₹15,000–₹75,000. Content, tools and link outreach are usually extra.

faqs.q: Is an SEO freelancer cheaper than an agency?
faqs.a: Per hour of senior attention, always. Per deliverable, only up to a point. Once you add the roughly ₹25,000/month of tools and writing a freelance quote assumes you'll buy yourself, a ₹35,000 freelancer costs ₹60,000 — and still has no link capacity and no cover during leave.

faqs.q: What do freelancers usually exclude from their quote?
faqs.a: Ahrefs or Semrush, a crawler licence, rank tracking, content writing, editing, developer time to implement fixes, and link outreach. Cover during illness or leave is excluded by definition. None of it is dishonest — it's assumed knowledge that founders rarely have.

faqs.q: When should I switch from a freelancer to an agency?
faqs.a: When technical fixes, content and link building all need to move in the same month, when your content calendar starts slipping because one person is the bottleneck, or when your budget crosses about ₹60,000 and you're still getting one person's part-time attention for it.

faqs.q: How do I protect myself if my freelancer disappears?
faqs.a: Own every account yourself — analytics, Search Console, CMS, registrar — and grant access rather than receive it. Keep one shared folder with the audit, keyword map and content calendar updated monthly. Agree 30 days' notice both ways in writing before the first invoice.

Advise on them, yes. Run outreach at volume, rarely — it's a full-time job on its own. If a sub-₹40,000 retainer promises links alongside technical and content work, ask exactly where those links come from. "Our network" means a private blog network and it's a penalty waiting to land.
